# Course exit after the current action

This is a new forecasting question on the Stanford SNAP MOOC user-action release. The OULAD day-60 analysis remains a separate population audit. Predict the externally recorded state label immediately after observing an action. A zero label represents the publisher's recorded outcome. The finite observation window limits interpretation of a learner's last event. [Dataset](https://snap.stanford.edu/data/act-mooc.html) · [Kumar, Zhang and Leskovec, KDD 2019](https://snap.stanford.edu/jodie/)

Use all actions in released order. Index the first 80% as fitting data, the next 10% as validation, and the last 10% as the sole evaluation. Floor boundaries as in JODIE. Keep repeat learners across periods for deployment on a continuing stream. Use only event data through the current row, without feeding any evaluation labels into subsequent forecasts. The four anonymized attributes lack a timestamp-level provenance guarantee. Interpret results as replay of published features.

Candidate is a convex blend of a gated recurrent unit on the most recent eight actions of the learner and gradient boosting on explicit current and historical features. The recurrent model receives activity IDs and the same numeric covariates for each of eight steps. The tree receives current features including learner activity count, previous item, time since preceding action, elapsed time since first action, repetition count for this item and numeric attributes. Tune the blend from weights 0, .25, .5, .75, 1 on validation ROC AUC. Fit two tree sizes (15 and 31 leaves, 200 iterations) and choose on validation. For the recurrent model train eight epochs and retain the highest validation AUC. Use a fixed seed (731), hidden size 32, Adam learning rate .001 and square-root inverse-frequency positive class weight fitted on training. Baselines in this first stage include both full components, an L2 logistic model using the tree inputs and a matched tree using only current activity, timestamp and four current attributes. Report micro AUC and average precision, predictions, class counts, and paired differences with intervals resampling whole evaluation learners. Each candidate must gain at least .01 AUC and a positive simultaneous lower endpoint versus every first-stage comparator. The original OULAD question had no predictor-superiority threshold. This margin applies only to the new action task.

A component tie or failed contrast eliminates this candidate. Only a surviving candidate advances to an aligned JODIE and temporal graph network comparison. Any such comparison must fit preprocessing on training, resolve availability of online labels, and produce paired predictions on identical actions. Published scalar AUCs on differently processed streams cannot substitute. A first-stage pass alone does not establish a winning paper.
